research_question: Does F2's omission of sqlite3.connect(autocommit=...) make its explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction contract depend on a Python default that is documented to change?

external_primary_sources.name: Python 3.13 sqlite3 documentation
external_primary_sources.observed: connect() exposes autocommit added in 3.12; current default is sqlite3.LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL and documentation says the default will change to False in a future release.

external_primary_sources.name: Python 3.14 sqlite3 documentation
external_primary_sources.observed: autocommit=False is recommended PEP-249 behavior and means sqlite3 keeps a transaction open, opening BEGIN DEFERRED on connect and immediately after commit/rollback. LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL retains pre-3.12 behavior.

external_primary_sources.name: Python 3.15.0rc1 sqlite3 documentation
external_primary_sources.observed: As of the current 3.15 release-candidate documentation, autocommit still defaults to LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL and still carries the future-change warning. Therefore the risk is prospective/ABI-drift, not evidence of a Python-3.15 break today.

exact_project_sources.observed: CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore.open calls sqlite3.connect(uri, uri=True, timeout=timeout) without autocommit/isolation_level. __init__ rejects connection.in_transaction, while initialize_schema/write_checkpoint explicitly issue BEGIN IMMEDIATE then use Connection.commit()/rollback().
Release artifacts must declare minimum runtime dependencies and support clean-machine/restart acceptance; dependency ABI drift is therefore part of product portability evidence.

findings.finding: F2 currently inherits Python sqlite3's LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL because it omits autocommit=. Python documents that this default will change to False in a future release.
findings.impact: Current behavior is version-default dependent rather than fully declared by F2 source.

findings.finding: Under autocommit=False, Python ensures a transaction is always open and uses BEGIN DEFERRED when opening one. F2 currently rejects an already-open transaction at store construction and later issues its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
findings.impact: If the Python default flips while F2 source remains unchanged, writer open is expected to fail closed at CALLER_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_OPEN; absent that guard, explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE would be at risk of nested-transaction failure. This is an inference from the two explicit contracts, not a target-runtime observation.

findings.finding: Python 3.15.0rc1 documentation still shows LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL as the default.
findings.impact: Do not report this as a present 3.15 incompatibility. The defect class is unpinned ABI/default dependence.

findings.finding: F2 should choose and test one transaction-control model rather than inherit the interpreter default: either preserve the existing explicit-SQL BEGIN IMMEDIATE style with an explicitly pinned compatible sqlite3 transaction mode, or refactor to PEP-249 autocommit=False semantics and remove assumptions that no transaction is open before each explicit BEGIN.
findings.impact: No recommendation to change product code is promoted until E2/E3 distinguishes the lowest-risk behavior-preserving option.

counterhypothesis.statement: The omitted autocommit parameter is harmless because Python sqlite3 defaults are stable enough for F2's portable lifetime.
counterhypothesis.remaining_uncertainty: The exact Python release that will flip the default is not specified by the current documentation.

candidate_delta.proposal: Bind Python version plus sqlite3 transaction-control mode into the runtime dependency receipt and make sqlite3.connect transaction mode explicit in the writer boundary. Preserve BEGIN IMMEDIATE semantics or deliberately migrate them; never allow an interpreter default change to select the concurrency contract silently.
candidate_delta.expected_benefit: Portable deterministic transaction semantics and fail-closed dependency drift.
candidate_delta.runtime_cost: Negligible; one explicit connection parameter/contract plus capability readback/tests.

negative_evidence: No current F2 target/VPS Python interpreter version was observed in this research stage.
No Python 3.15 current default break was found; current RC1 documentation retains LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL.
No production code was changed or runtime acceptance executed.
The exact future Python release changing the default remains unspecified.
next_discriminator: E2 map the smallest behavior-preserving explicit transaction-mode contract onto CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore, then E3 locally compare current omitted-default behavior with explicit LEGACY/manual and autocommit=False modes.
